candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a large ill-defined hypoechoic mass involving the upper pole of the left thyroid lobe with internal coarse calcification that is contiguous with the hypopharynx, along with coarse calcification in lymph nodes and a poorly differentiated malignant tumour on FNA — features pointing to anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) invading the hypopharynx/pyriform fossa rather than a primary hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. C001 asserts the pyriform fossa mass as the primary site, which conflicts with the reference diagnosis of ATC originating from the thyroid.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies a hypopharyngeal primary rather than a thyroid primary

case_quality_flags: Classic ATC presentation: rapidly enlarging thyroid mass with laryngeal fixation, coarse calcification on ultrasound, poorly differentiated histology, and distant bony metastasis — distinguishable from primary hypopharyngeal SCC by thyroid lobe involvement and calcification pattern
